title: Canary weave + approval flow for safe auto-adopt of Optimize recommendations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an orchestration layer that safely auto-applies Redwood Optimize (batching/caching/quantization) recommendations using a configurable canary weave and approval lattice. This ticket implements the controller, policy DSL, and Console/CLI hooks required to: 1) perform dry-run simulations, 2) deploy staged canaries across traffic slices, 3) gate expansions on cost and quality signals, and 4) surface approvals and audit logs for compliance. Goal: enable low-risk automatic adoption for low-risk recommendations while preserving operator control for higher-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a dry-run mode that simulates a recommendation application with an estimated cost delta and list of affected routes (no env changes)
Canary weave supports at minimum: initial shadow apply, 1% traffic test, 10% ramp, 50% ramp, full apply; each step configurable via policy DSL
Automated gates evaluate both cost delta (expected token/unit savings) and quality regressions (prompt set evals) and can pause or rollback an expansion
Manual approval step visible in Console with contextual artifacts (PRD link, diff, expected savings, A/B eval metrics) and an approver audit trail
Automatic rollback triggers on threshold violations: latency regression > 10%, quality drop > configurable threshold, or error-rate spike > configured SLO deviation
All apply/rollback operations produce structured audit logs (operator, time, diff, reason) stored to customer audit trail and platform event store
Integration tests exercise a synthetic canary with injected metric regressions and verify rollback behavior
Metrics and dashboards added to Console showing per-canary cost delta, latency, and quality signals for 90d history
tasks: Design: author a short spec for the policy DSL (scopes, gates, thresholds, cadence) and share with PM/Design
Infra: add a controller deployment + RBAC roles for autoadopt workflows
Engine: implement dry-run engine that computes token-level cost delta and affected routes without changing runtime configs
Orchestrator: create the 'canary weave' state machine (shadow -> staged traffic -> ramp -> done/rollback)
Gating: implement gate evaluators for cost delta, eval-quality, latency, error-rate and a generic threshold API
Console: UI for approvals, canary status, and one-click abort/revert; include link to dry-run artifact
CLI: add commands to list pending autoadopt workflows and to manually approve/abort
Observability: add traces, structured events, and a dedicated per-canary dashboard; hook alerts for gate violations
Testing: unit tests for DSL parser, integration tests for canary state transitions, chaos test that simulates node failures during ramp
Docs: runbook for operators and SREs describing how to triage staged rollouts and how to trigger manual rollbacks
risks: Incorrect cost delta estimation could cause false-positive adoptings leading to degraded user cost/latency
Incomplete eval coverage for quality regressions — some regressions could escape the gate if prompt set is insufficient
Race conditions during concurrent applies if two recommendations touch overlapping route configs
Operator confusion if UI/approval flows are not concise — could lead to accidental approvals
Audit/logging gaps could fail compliance requirements for enterprise customers
qa_plan: Create a synthetic tenant with mirrored traffic for shadow applies
Run canary scenarios with controlled regressions for latency/quality and assert rollback
Verify dry-run outputs match actual post-apply deltas within an acceptable margin (5%)
Manual acceptance tests for Console approval UX with product/solutions engineering
Security review of audit logs and RBAC before enabling autoapply in production tenants
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only for staging tenants — limited to non-critical models and routes
Beta: opt-in by select customers via feature flag (customer success + AE cohort) — collect feedback
GA: enabled for 'low-risk' recommendation classes with conservative thresholds and operator approvals by default
Escalation: provide single-click global abort and tenant-scoped revert tools for SRE/ops
Post-GA: expand recommendation classes and relax thresholds as confidence grows
